chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Barqi, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his father, from Ali (peace be upon him) who said:

The maintenance (nafaqah) of the pregnant woman whose husband has died is paid from all the estate until she gives birth. The interpretation of this report is one of two matters: either it is understood as recommended (mustahabb) if the heirs agree to it, or the correct view is that she is maintained from all the estate because the share of the fetus has not yet been distinguished; it is only distinguished when she gives birth and it is known whether it is male or female. At that point, his estate is partitioned. When it is distinguished, what was spent on her is taken from her share and returned to the heirs. The benefit of this report is that maintenance is not obligatory upon one heir to the exclusion of the other, but they are equal in this matter.
ai.seo_question: How is a pregnant widow's maintenance paid from the estate before the child's gender is known?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi presents two scholarly interpretations for this ruling: either the expenditure is merely recommended (mustahabb) if heirs agree, or it is obligatory because the fetus's share is undifferentiated until birth. This ensures that the maintenance burden is shared equally among all heirs rather than falling on one, with the cost later deducted from the child's specific inheritance portion once its gender and share are determined.
